messages.subject: backtransform for categorical and continuous variables

Hello everyone,

I have fitted several models using distsamp that includes categorical and continuous variables (in big part thanks to this group!). I choose the best model for my data based on Akaike weights and now I am want to plot the results. The selected model has one categorical (habitat type, four categories) and one continuous site covariate (elevation) . However, I am a bit confuse on how to use "backTransform"  when having model like this. What I know is that that I have to use linearComb together with backTransform. I think I might be overlooking an example that make things clear for me, but I have not seen one that includes both categorical and continuous variable when using backTransform:

1) How should I set up my matrix? 
2) Is it necessary to use backTransform before predict? I believe it is because I used predict and plotted the results (as a test) and I got truly weird and unreasonable results! I hope the problem is not using backTransform first.

Thank you all very much for your time and attention. An answer on this matter would really help me move forward with my analyses!! 

Best wishes,

Laura

What model type are you using?  Either way, the predict function should work here.  Richard illustrates this in section 5 of the distsamp vignette.
